A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CAKE research paper, with complete main text and Appendices A–J. Text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LongBench and NeedleBench experiments, memory and latency measurements, ablations, and attention analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithm 1 and Appendix C retain the same preference metric, adaptive allocation, cascading cache management and mean-plus-variance eviction indicator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 16 LongBench datasets and NeedleBench retrieval and reasoning tasks, including the same English and Chinese coverage in Appendix G.

E2.justification: LongBench retains StreamingLLM, H2O, TOVA, SnapKV and PyramidKV. NeedleBench retains H2O, SnapKV and PyramidKV, while Appendix E retains the KIVI and KCVC quantization comparisons.

E3.justification: The model configurations, cache budgets, context lengths and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix G retains Levenshtein-based scoring, and Appendix H retains the fixed 1,024-token generation setting.

E4.justification: The allocation and eviction-indicator ablations in Section 5.6, component and temperature studies in Appendix I, quantization compatibility experiments in Appendix E, and attention analyses in Appendix J are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that each NeedleBench case is repeated ten times and retain the random-allocation result of 28.3 ± 0.2 in Table 2. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedures change.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, CAKE retains the 29.29 LongBench average for Llama2-7B at budget 128L in Table 1 and the 71.87 Mistral NeedleBench 32K overall score at 1024L in Table 10.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 1, Theorem 1 and Appendix D proofs are unchanged, including monotonic budget reduction and the equivalence of cascading and single-step eviction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims, including preservation of performance with 3.2% of the cache and over 10× decoding speedup at 128K context.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and qualifications are retained. These include Appendix B's limitation concerning within-layer attention dynamics and Appendix G's discussion of multi-needle retrieval degradation under extremely small cache budgets.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the temperature-search ranges, gamma = 200, 32-token observation window and implementation pseudocode. The A100 80GB hardware disclosure and code-access information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning, including comparisons with uniform and pyramid-shaped allocation and discussion of complementary compression methods.

P1.justification: The page-11 acknowledgement now specifies Ant Group support through the CCF-Ant Research Fund, while retaining the same NSFC grants. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–15, Tables 1–14, Algorithm 1 and Listing 1 retain their content, visual structure and placement. There is no figure, table or substantive page-layout revision.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the funding acknowledgement, but the scientific content, evidence, proofs, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged throughout the paper and appendices. This administrative clarification does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
